decisions.reason: Its delayed and geographically limited rollout, followed by only a brief mention rather than sustained standalone promotion, makes it easier even for commitment-prone management to attribute lower traction to a niche offering and reallocate resources.

As a core dosimetry chamber backed by the firm's longstanding measurement expertise and given dedicated promotion across two years, management would likely continue supporting it and justify weaker signals as temporary market adoption issues.

Because it sits squarely within the firm's established ionization-chamber business and received visible post-launch commitment, escalation of commitment makes continued commercialization more likely than withdrawal.

A standard clinical ionization chamber is central to the firm's core customer needs and publicly launched presence, so management would be inclined to persist rather than concede that the launch underperformed.

This relative-dosimetry chamber complements the firm's calibration and QA portfolio, and prior investment plus strategic fit would encourage management to keep it on the market despite limited later evidence.

The thimble chamber is a conventional, portfolio-consistent product with clear synergies to the firm's service and measurement capabilities, which under an escalation-of-commitment logic favors retention.
